<reason>Both sides fought a genuinely narrowed clash: PRO on reliability/validity and the "label is the product" reframe, CON on burden asymmetry (one defensible use survives), the counterfactual (gut feel replaces the inventory), and the retreat as a non-forecasting context. CON's thermometer/rounding analogy and the "non-evaluative frame" point were its best original work, and "replaceability is not invalidity" was a clean late frame. But PRO controlled the two decisive pivots. First, PRO's dilemma — if only the continuous scores are accurate, you are describing a Big Five inventory, not MBTI/DISC — forced CON to relocate the distinctive value into the letters, after which CON's own line "the letters open the conversation; the specifics carry it" handed PRO the argument that the usable content survives removal of the typology. Second, PRO's pressure question extracted a costly honest concession: results should shape interview probes, onboarding, and team placement, which PRO immediately weaponized ("a rounding error near a midpoint picks someone's first manager") and CON never defended again, effectively ceding the hiring half of the motion in its closing. CON's burden framing (need only one surviving use) is legitimate and kept it competitive, but the residual benefit it defended — that coarse letters uniquely license disclosure — was asserted mechanism against PRO's plausible alternatives (facilitator-led feedback rounds, "working with me" one-pagers) and PRO's harm story that a stereotype displaces the specific self-report. Grounding was disciplined on both sides, with no fake citations. PRO also made the decision easier by stating a usable standard (tools that assert facts about persons must back them) and showing every named benefit surviving the ban.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's turn on CON's own phrase "the letters open the conversation; the specifics carry it" — pairing it with CON's admitted hiring use (shaping team placement) to show the value sits in the non-MBTI part while the decision-moving part is the unreliable label. CON's reply that "no answer can be wrong means nobody is ranked, not that nothing is measured" was a fair patch but arrived only in closing and left the hiring concession undefended.</best_rebuttal>
